evidence_items.summary: This chapter explores the impact of Generative Artificial Intelligence (GAI) on students’ oral discourse during the defence of Final Degree Projects (Trabajo Fin de Título or TFT, in Spanish). It addresses a significant gap in research by focusing on GAI’s influence on spoken language, particularly in academic contexts like dissertation defences. The chapter also aims to establish criteria for evaluating oral defences in Spanish universities, with a special focus on GAI’s role in their preparation. Based on a review of literature from Scopus and Dialnet, and a comparison of evaluation criteria across fifteen Spanish universities, the chapter proposes key indicators for assessing these defences. It identifies six core competences for evaluation: communication skills, language use, structure and coherence, time management, use of visual aids, and handling questions. Also, it suggests specific GAI-related signs (e.g. impersonal language, repetitive sentences, or unclear use of sources) to detect AI-generated content that could affect the assessment of TFT. The chapter emphasises the importance of ethical GAI use in oral presentations and concludes with proposals for the responsible integration of this technology into education to help students and educators reach their full potential. Book title: Ethical Challenges of AI in Academia: Impact and Implications for Higher Education Edited by: Peter Lang, ISBN: 9783631941270

evidence_items.summary: Abstract: Efficient sensing remains critical in low-cost Internet of Things (IoT) and Web of Things (WoT)-enabled edge nodes, even when the sensor itself is inexpensive and widely used. The DHT11 temperature and humidity sensor employs a single-wire dig-ital protocol and relies on Arduino libraries for data acquisition, timeout handling, and scheduling behavior. In this paper, eight Arduino DHT11 libraries are benchmarked on an Arduino Uno R3 using six criteria: flash memory usage, SRAM consumption, average measured call duration, timing variability, maximum CPU blocking time, and failure-recovery behavior. The results reveal substantial performance trade-offs. Aver-age measured call durations ranged from 5,588 µs for the asynchronous DHT Sensors Non-Blocking implementation to approximately 1.04 s for DHT11; however, these measurements reflect different execution semantics and should not be interpreted as directly equivalent end-to-end acquisition latencies. Flash usage ranged from 4,288 to 5,244 bytes, while SRAM consumption ranged from 238 to 266 bytes. TroykaDHT and SDHT delivered the most stable low-latency readings, DFRobot DHT11 minimized SRAM usage, and DHT Sensors Non-Blocking was most suitable when asynchronous execution and reduced continuous CPU occupation were required. This study does not directly benchmark application-layer protocols or cloud services, such as HTTP, MQTT, REST, or WebSocket; instead, it characterizes sensing-layer behavior that can influence data freshness, task scheduling, and overall responsiveness in resource-constrained IoT/WoT edge deployments.
evidence_items.title: Performance Analysis of Arduino DHT11 Sensor Libraries for Resource-constrained IoT/WoT Edge Nodes.

evidence_items.summary: This study combines a historical and analytical review of economic growth theory with an institutional analysis. Five approaches to the quality of economic growth are systematised, and a conceptual framework is developed that links formal and informal institutions to growth outcomes through market mechanisms. The framework is then examined using national data for 2016–2025 and a 2025 comparative benchmark covering five Central Asian economies, based on official statistics and international indices. Uzbekistan's real GDP growth accelerated to 7.7% in 2025, while the national poverty rate declined from 11.0% in 2023 to 5.8% in 2025. At the same time, the Corruption Perceptions Index score changed from 33 to 31 over the corresponding two-year period, indicators related to government accountability continue to demonstrate potential for further improvement, and the non-observed economy is estimated at approximately one-third of GDP. The paper characterises this pattern as an "institutional lag", referring to a situation in which improvements in economic growth and social outcomes are occurring more rapidly than the development of the institutional foundations supporting market mechanisms. Regional benchmarking further indicates that the highest economic growth rates in Central Asia do not necessarily coincide with the strongest institutional indicators.
evidence_items.title: INSTITUTIONAL ENVIRONMENT AND THE QUALITY OF ECONOMIC GROWTH: A CONCEPTUAL FRAMEWORK AND EVIDENCE FROM UZBEKISTAN
